title: CloudWatch metrics (namespaces, dimensions, and custom metrics)
hook: Amazon CloudWatch metrics are time-series data points identified by namespace, metric name, and dimensions. AWS services publish automatically; your applications emit custom metrics — but high-cardinality dimensions can explode cost.

blocks.text: Metrics live in namespaces like AWS/Lambda or Custom/Orders. Dimensions are key-value filters — FunctionName, QueueName. Statistics include Sum, Average, p99 via extended statistics. PutMetricData publishes custom points; Embedded Metric Format (EMF) extracts metrics from structured logs without separate API calls.

blocks.text: You cannot debug what you do not measure. SQS ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage is the lag SLA metric. Custom metrics per userId bankrupt the account. Senior engineers design metric hierarchies: aggregate in metrics, drill in logs.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: namespace + name + dimensions. Low cardinality dimensions. EMF from Lambda logs. Alarm on age and error rate not raw counts alone.

snippet.label: TypeScript — EMF structured log metric
snippet.explanation: CloudWatch extracts OrdersProcessed without PutMetricData charges per call pattern.

snippet.label: CLI — query SQS lag metric
snippet.code:
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics \
  --namespace AWS/SQS \
  --metric-name ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage \
  --dimensions Name=QueueName,Value=orders \
  --start-time $(date -u -v-1H +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) \
  --end-time $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) \
  --period 60 --statistics Maximum
snippet.explanation: Maximum statistic catches worst-case lag in each minute — better for SLA than Average.

snippet.label: TypeScript — PutMetricData with low cardinality
snippet.explanation: Only Environment dimension — not per-orderId. Use logs for per-order drill-down.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — alarm with metric math error rate
snippet.code:
Resources:
  ErrorRateAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      AlarmName: payment-processor-error-rate
      Metrics:
        - Id: errors
          MetricStat:
            Metric:
              Namespace: AWS/Lambda
              MetricName: Errors
              Dimensions:
                - Name: FunctionName
                  Value: payment-processor
            Period: 60
            Stat: Sum
        - Id: invocations
          MetricStat:
            Metric:
              Namespace: AWS/Lambda
              MetricName: Invocations
              Dimensions:
                - Name: FunctionName
                  Value: payment-processor
            Period: 60
            Stat: Sum
        - Id: errorRate
          Expression: (errors / invocations) * 100
      Threshold: 5
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanThreshold
      EvaluationPeriods: 2
snippet.explanation: Metric math alarm on percentage — scales with traffic volume unlike raw error count.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: userId as dimension. Alarm on raw Errors without normalizing by Invocations. Average on latency when p99 matters. Missing Maximum on AgeOfOldestMessage.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: Cost Explorer custom metrics line; dimension count audit script. SQS dashboard: AgeOfOldestMessage + NumberOfMessagesVisible + NumberOfMessagesDeleted rate. Lambda INSIGHTS for enhanced metrics. High-resolution metrics (1-second) cost more — enable only during incidents.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying 'emit a metric per user for dashboards.' Strong answer: aggregate metrics low cardinality; per-user in Logs Insights or data warehouse.

interviewTakeaways: Metrics = namespace + name + dimensions; AWS services auto-publish to AWS/* namespaces.
Avoid high-cardinality dimensions — aggregate per tenant/environment.
EMF in Lambda logs extracts custom metrics without per-call PutMetricData.
60s: AgeOfOldestMessage for SQS lag. Error rate metric math. Low cardinality. EMF from logs.
commonPitfalls: Per-userId PutMetricData — cost explosion rejection answer.
Strong answer: tenant-level aggregate metrics, user detail in logs.
Alarm raw error count on variable traffic.
Using Average for queue age SLA instead of Maximum.
